annotations.description:
The annotations to associate with this application. Annotations may be used to store client information, but are not used by the server. 

**Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the annotations present in your configuration.
Please refer to the field 'effective_annotations' for all of the annotations present on the resource.
annotations.rationale: Annotations are non-authoritative metadata used for client information and do not directly configure the application's security posture.

application_environment.description: An ApplicationEnvironment from which to inherit configuration properties.
application_environment.rationale: Selects an application environment from which configuration is inherited. The appropriate environment is workload-specific rather than a universal security policy target.

deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: Controls Terraform resource lifecycle behaviour during deletion. Whether a Spark application should be deleted, abandoned, or protected from Terraform destruction is an operational lifecycle decision rather than a platform security control.

dependency_images.description: List of container image uris for additional file dependencies. Dependent files are sequentially copied from each image. If a file with the same name exists in 2 images then the file from later image is used.
dependency_images.rationale: Specifies container images whose files are copied into the application environment. Untrusted or unapproved dependency images can introduce malicious or vulnerable executable content, so image sources should be restricted to approved locations.

display_name.description: User-provided human-readable name to be used in user interfaces.
display_name.rationale: Provides a human-readable display name for user interfaces and does not directly affect access control, data protection, or execution security.

labels.description:
The labels to associate with this application. Labels may be used for filtering and billing tracking. 

**Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the labels present in your configuration.
Please refer to the field 'effective_labels' for all of the labels present on the resource.
labels.rationale: Labels are non-authoritative metadata primarily used for filtering, organisation, and billing and do not directly configure the application's security posture.

location.description: The location of the spark application.
location.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).

namespace.description: The Kubernetes namespace in which to create the application. This namespace must already exist on the cluster.
namespace.rationale: Determines the Kubernetes namespace in which the application is created. Namespace placement can affect isolation, access controls, service accounts, policies, and exposure, so deployments should be restricted to approved namespaces.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: Identifies the Google Cloud project containing the resource. The correct project is deployment-specific and is not by itself a universal security configuration for the Spark application.

properties.rationale: Application-specific Spark properties can alter runtime behaviour and security-relevant configuration. Unsafe property values may weaken protections or change execution behaviour, so security-sensitive properties should be governed.

serviceinstance.description: The id of the service instance to which this spark application belongs.
serviceinstance.rationale: Identifies the Dataproc service instance to which the application belongs. The required service instance is environment-specific rather than a universal security policy setting.

spark_application_id.rationale: Provides the identifier for the Spark application and does not directly control its security posture.

version.description: The Dataproc version of this application.
version.rationale: Selects the Dataproc application version. Version choice depends on compatibility and lifecycle requirements and is not suitable for a universal static security policy without an organisation-defined approved-version baseline.

pyspark_application_config.archive_uris.description: HCFS URIs of archives to be extracted into the working directory of each executor. Supported file types: .jar, .tar, .tar.gz, .tgz, and .zip.
pyspark_application_config.archive_uris.rationale: Specifies external archives extracted into executor working directories. Untrusted archives can introduce executable or malicious content, so dependency sources should be restricted to approved locations.

pyspark_application_config.args.description: The arguments to pass to the driver.  Do not include arguments, such as '--conf', that can be set as job properties, since a collision may occur that causes an incorrect job submission.
pyspark_application_config.args.rationale: Driver arguments influence application execution and may contain unsafe runtime parameters or sensitive values. Restricting dangerous argument patterns can reduce insecure execution configurations.

pyspark_application_config.file_uris.description: HCFS URIs of files to be placed in the working directory of each executor. Useful for naively parallel tasks.
pyspark_application_config.file_uris.rationale: Specifies external files copied into executor working directories. Untrusted file sources can introduce malicious or unintended content and should therefore be restricted to approved locations.

pyspark_application_config.jar_file_uris.description: HCFS URIs of jar files to add to the CLASSPATHs of the Python driver and tasks.
pyspark_application_config.jar_file_uris.rationale: Specifies JAR dependencies added to driver and task classpaths. Because JARs contain executable code, untrusted sources can introduce malicious code and should be restricted.

pyspark_application_config.main_python_f.description: The HCFS URI of the main Python file to use as the driver. Must be a .py file.
pyspark_application_config.main_python_f.rationale: Identifies the main Python program executed by the application. Because this directly selects executable code, the URI should be restricted to trusted and approved sources.

pyspark_application_config.python_file_u.description: HCFS file URIs of Python files to pass to the PySpark framework. Supported file types: .py, .egg, and .zip.
pyspark_application_config.python_file_u.rationale: Specifies Python code and package dependencies supplied to PySpark. Untrusted Python files, eggs, or archives can execute malicious code and should be restricted to approved sources.

spark_application_config.archive_uris.description: HCFS URIs of archives to be extracted into the working directory of each executor. Supported file types: '.jar', '.tar', '.tar.gz', '.tgz', and '.zip'.
spark_application_config.archive_uris.rationale: Specifies archives extracted into executor working directories. Untrusted archives can introduce malicious executable content, so archive sources should be restricted to approved locations.

spark_application_config.args.description: The arguments to pass to the driver. Do not include arguments that can be set as application properties, such as '--conf', since a collision can occur that causes an incorrect application submission.
spark_application_config.args.rationale: Driver arguments influence Spark application execution and can introduce unsafe runtime behaviour or sensitive values, making dangerous argument patterns security relevant.

spark_application_config.file_uris.description: HCFS URIs of files to be placed in the working directory of each executor.
spark_application_config.file_uris.rationale: Specifies files copied into executor working directories. Untrusted sources can introduce malicious or unintended content and should be restricted to approved locations.

spark_application_config.jar_file_uris.description: HCFS URIs of jar files to add to the classpath of the Spark driver and tasks.
spark_application_config.jar_file_uris.rationale: Specifies JAR files added to the Spark classpath. JARs contain executable code, so untrusted dependencies can introduce malicious behaviour and should be restricted.

spark_application_config.main_class.description: The name of the driver main class. The jar file that contains the class must be in the classpath or specified in 'jar_file_uris'.
spark_application_config.main_class.rationale: Specifies the Java or Scala driver class within the supplied application code. The required class name is application-specific and cannot be governed by a universal platform security allowlist.

spark_application_config.main_jar_file_u.description: The HCFS URI of the jar file that contains the main class.
spark_application_config.main_jar_file_u.rationale: Identifies the main JAR containing executable application code. Untrusted JAR sources can execute malicious code and should be restricted to approved locations.

spark_r_application_config.archive_uris.description: HCFS URIs of archives to be extracted into the working directory of each executor. Supported file types: .jar, .tar, .tar.gz, .tgz, and .zip.
spark_r_application_config.archive_uris.rationale: Specifies archives extracted into executor working directories. Untrusted archives can introduce malicious content, so archive sources should be restricted to approved locations.

spark_r_application_config.args.description: The arguments to pass to the driver.  Do not include arguments, such as '--conf', that can be set as job properties, since a collision may occur that causes an incorrect job submission.
spark_r_application_config.args.rationale: Driver arguments influence SparkR execution and can introduce unsafe runtime behaviour or sensitive values, making dangerous argument patterns security relevant.

spark_r_application_config.file_uris.description: HCFS URIs of files to be placed in the working directory of each executor. Useful for naively parallel tasks.
spark_r_application_config.file_uris.rationale: Specifies files copied into executor working directories. Untrusted file sources can introduce malicious or unintended content and should be restricted.

spark_r_application_config.main_r_file_u.description: The HCFS URI of the main R file to use as the driver. Must be a .R file.
spark_r_application_config.main_r_file_u.rationale: Identifies the main R program executed by the application. Because this directly selects executable code, the URI should be restricted to trusted and approved sources.

spark_sql_application_config.jar_file_ur.description: HCFS URIs of jar files to be added to the Spark CLASSPATH.
spark_sql_application_config.jar_file_ur.rationale: Specifies JAR dependencies added to the Spark SQL classpath. Since JARs contain executable code, untrusted dependencies can introduce malicious behaviour and should be restricted.

spark_sql_application_config.query_file_.description: The HCFS URI of the script that contains SQL queries.
spark_sql_application_config.query_file_.rationale: Identifies a SQL script executed by the application. An untrusted script can perform unintended data access or modification, so the script source should be restricted to approved locations.

spark_sql_application_config.script_vari.description: Mapping of query variable names to values (equivalent to the Spark SQL command: SET 'name="value";').
spark_sql_application_config.script_vari.rationale: Supplies values consumed by Spark SQL scripts. These values can influence executed queries and may expose sensitive information or alter data operations, making their use security relevant.

spark_sql_application_config.query_list..rationale: Contains SQL statements executed by the application. Queries can read, modify, or expose data, so unsafe query content can directly affect security and data protection.
